name: Eric J. Goossen
headline: Computer engineering student at the University of Washington focused on embodied intelligence, where machine learning meets the real world.
description: Eric J. Goossen: computer engineering student at the University of Washington focused on embodied intelligence, where machine learning meets the real world.
bio: I'm a computer engineering student at the University of Washington with experience in three robotics labs, building the software that makes robots reliable: controllers, planners, simulators, and evaluation infrastructure.

I co-authored research at the Human Centered Robotics Lab showing human feedback lifts Code-as-Policies 1.75× over base VLAs, work on the undergrad team at the Personal Robotics Lab building software for an NVIDIA-granted bimanual robot, and am working toward a paper on fleet-parallel RL at WEIRD Lab. Outside the labs, I program control and localization for ARUW, UW's RoboMaster team, and build Achilles, a SIMD-batched rigid-body simulator for faster RL training.
I'm motivated by turning abstract math and computer science into reliable, real-world systems with measurable impact.
